Every one of the 435 cited declarations exists at the pinned commits, and no target marked absent was found in either library, so every layer verdict stands. 44 findings: 1 high, 16 medium, 27 low. The high one: HC.3 (and HR.5) cite PowerSeries.HasSubst as matching the layers' topological-nilpotence hypothesis, but HasSubst requires algebraic nilpotence of the constant coefficient; the matching API is PowerSeries.HasEval/aeval, with Tau Ceti's PowerSeries.aeval_subst as the bridge. The medium ones are library results the audit misses (Tau Ceti's maximalIntegralCurve for HopfRinow layer 1, Mathlib's class-number-one certificate and Tau Ceti's A(S,2) descent bound for ComputationalNumberTheory, Habiro's cyclotomic congruence in Mathlib, Tau Ceti's integral Krull-dimension results and AdjoinRoot.equivPiFactors), false details in notes (P_N is not monic; the R[q] → R[q]^S injectivity needs only S ≠ ∅), and duplicate lists that name consumers instead of duplicates or miss the real owners.

PowerSeries.HasSubst requires the constant coefficient to be nilpotent in the algebraic sense, and the substitution API gives the coefficient ring the discrete topology. So PowerSeries.subst/substAlgHom/subst_comp_subst cannot define these maps. The Mathlib API that matches the layer's hypothesis, evaluation at a topologically nilpotent element of a complete separated linearly topologised algebra, is not cited. Tau Ceti's bridge between the two APIs, and its evaluation estimates over adic rings, are not cited either.
